questions.prompt: Explain why a person with myopia needs a concave lens, including what happens to the light with and without it.
questions.modelAnswer: In myopia, light from distant objects is focused in front of the retina because the eye’s lens system is too strong or the eyeball too long, so the image is blurred. A concave lens diverges the light slightly before it enters the eye, so the eye focuses it further back, exactly on the retina. Its focal length equals the far point (P = −1/far point).
rubric: Without: focus in front of the retina
